answer: I would like to describe a small act of kindness that has stayed with me for years. A few years ago I was travelling alone to Chattogram for a job interview, and on my first evening I got hopelessly lost, with a dying phone and no idea where my hotel was. The streets all looked the same in the dark, and I was starting to panic. A middle-aged stranger, who turned out to be a local schoolteacher, noticed me looking anxious and stopped to ask if I needed help. What struck me was how genuinely [[considerate]] he was; not only did he give me directions, he actually walked me halfway there. He could easily have ignored me, as most people would have, so his kindness felt almost [[remarkable]]. Along the way we chatted, and he told me a little about the area, which turned a stressful moment into a pleasant one. He even recommended a small tea stall near my hotel, which I went back to every day that week. I was incredibly [[grateful]], and I remember trying to offer him something in return, which he politely refused. That small act of kindness has genuinely stayed with me, and it made me more willing to help strangers myself, especially students who come into our office looking lost and nervous. It was a reminder that a little [[compassion]] costs nothing but can mean a great deal. I never even learned his name, but I still think of him fondly.

followUps.answer: I try to, in small ways. If someone looks lost or needs directions, I usually stop. After my own experience, I know how [[disorienting]] it feels to be alone somewhere completely unfamiliar.

followUps.q: Do you think people are less helpful to strangers nowadays?
followUps.answer: In big cities, perhaps a little, because everyone is in a hurry and slightly suspicious. But in smaller towns like mine, people still stop to help, and I find that very reassuring.

note: Made the unfamiliar city Chattogram (job interview trip), added who he was, the tea stall detail, a link to students at my office and a closing line.
